threads.thread_goal: Align on vision, target segments, and MVP scope for the platform.

messages.text:
Kicking off the eco-tourism platform work here. We need to align on who we are building for first and what absolutely needs to be in the MVP.

In project_pack_ref: Launch of Integrated Eco-Tourism Experience Platform, A1 already sketches target segments and a first pass at MVP scope, and T1, T3, T4 are the core work items.

Ask to the product managers: can one of you take the lead on consolidating a clear proposal for primary customer segments and priority regions, and another on translating that into a crisp MVP feature list? I would like us to converge on both this week so we can keep the 90-day delivery constraint realistic.

Thanks for framing this. I can take the lead on the segment and region proposal for T1 and also draft the first version of the journey for T3, then sync with others on MVP scope.

Initial thought based on A1: we seem to be leaning toward two main groups: urban professionals looking for short, high-quality nature breaks, and more committed eco-travelers willing to travel further and stay longer. For regions, A1 mentions coastal and forest destinations but not yet a clear priority.

Before I draft, can we confirm any hard constraints on regions for the first 90 days, for example existing partner relationships or regulatory readiness?

From the tourism side, I can support with region prioritisation and how that translates into concrete experiences.

Based on our current partners and what is realistic for an MVP, I would suggest we focus on two types of regions: 1) coastal marine conservation areas where we already have community-based operators, and 2) forest or mountain protected areas with existing low-impact trails.

For the first 90 days, I would avoid destinations where we do not yet have vetted partners under the criteria that will go into A3 and T6. That will keep us compliant and aligned with the conservation and community principles in the project_pack_ref: Launch of Integrated Eco-Tourism Experience Platform.

I can help on the MVP feature list for T4 and make sure it lines up with the financial and KPI side later.

Looking at A1, I see a mix of discovery, booking, payment, and post-trip features. To keep the 90-day constraint, I suggest we start by mapping only what is strictly needed to support the core journeys that will be in A4.

I will need clarity from you all on which customer segments we lock in for D1 before I finalise the feature list for D2, otherwise we risk overbuilding.

Happy to support on T4 as well, especially around how we present the product bundles and pricing on the platform.

From a commercial angle, I would like us to keep the MVP focused on a small number of clearly differentiated bundles per region, so the feature set can stay lean: search or browse by theme, simple comparison, and a straightforward booking flow.

Once we have the segment and region proposal from T1, I can sketch how those bundles might appear in the interface and what data we need to capture for later sales analysis.

On constraints: from a company strategy perspective, we should prioritise regions where we already have at least some partner relationships and basic legal checks done.

So for D1, I would like the proposal to assume: 1) one coastal region and 1) one forest or mountain region, both in markets where we already operate in other lines of business. That will reduce regulatory and operational risk.

If you can reflect that in T1 and the journey work in T3, we will be in a better position to keep the MVP within 90 days.

I can help by pulling together a short summary of the target segments and regions once we agree, so we can share it with the broader organisation.

For T1, I will wait for the proposal from 99087 and 52126, then I can turn that into a simple internal brief that also highlights the main expectations for partners and customer support.

This should also help when we later align with leadership on T9.

Understood. I will draft T1 assuming two primary segments and two priority regions as you described.

Working proposal for D1, to validate with you and 52126:
- Segment 1: time-constrained urban professionals, 30 to 50, looking for 3 to 5 day nature breaks with clear sustainability credentials.
- Segment 2: eco-enthusiasts willing to travel 7 to 10 days, open to more immersive community-based stays.

Regions: 1 coastal conservation area and 1 forest or mountain protected area in markets where we already have some presence. I will specify the exact regions in the T1 doc and link them back to the journeys in A4.

If this direction sounds right, I will move ahead and share a draft for comments before we call D1.

The two segments and the two-region approach make sense from a tourism and operations standpoint.

For the coastal region, I suggest we focus on an area where we already have community-led marine tours and homestays that meet the sustainability criteria we will formalise in A3 and T6. For the forest or mountain region, we should pick a protected area with existing low-impact trails and local guides.

Once you have the T1 draft, I can review and add concrete examples of experiences that fit each segment, which will also feed into T2 later.

With those segments and regions, I can start shaping the MVP feature list in T4.

My initial thought for D2 is that the MVP should at least cover:
- Discovery: browse by region and theme, basic filters by trip length and difficulty.
- Booking: simple date selection, party size, and confirmation.
- Payment: secure online payment with basic currency support.
- Post-trip: simple feedback capture so we can feed A4 and later A8.

I will keep anything like loyalty, advanced personalisation, or complex bundles for later releases unless we see a strong reason to include them now.

Agree with that outline. To keep scope tight for D2, I would also suggest we limit the number of filters and avoid any complex comparison tools in the MVP.

From a pricing and sales perspective, as long as we can show clear inclusions, exclusions, and total price per person, we can start learning quickly.

I will add a short note into T4 on how we present bundles and pricing so that it is consistent with what will go into A2 later.

The segment and region framing looks aligned with our strategy.

Let us formalise D1 as follows: primary customer segments are 1) time-constrained urban professionals seeking 3 to 5 day eco-breaks and 2) eco-enthusiasts seeking 7 to 10 day immersive trips. Priority regions are one coastal conservation area and one forest or mountain protected area in existing markets where we already operate.

Please capture this in T1 and reflect it in the journey work in A4 and T3.

Acknowledged on D1. I will update T1 with the confirmed segments and regions and ensure the journey map in A4 and T3 reflects both paths clearly.

Next, I will draft the end-to-end journey from discovery to post-trip feedback for each segment, highlighting where the MVP features you are discussing in T4 need to support key moments.

With D1 confirmed, I will refine the MVP feature list in T4 and map each feature to specific steps in the journey from A4.

For D2, my proposal is that the MVP feature set includes only what is needed to support: 1) discovery and selection of a small set of curated bundles in the two regions, 2) booking and payment, and 3) basic post-trip feedback.

Anything related to advanced personalisation, loyalty, or complex partner tools would be explicitly tagged as post-MVP in A5 later.

That framing for D2 is in line with our time and budget constraints.

Let us confirm D2 as: the MVP feature set will cover discovery and selection of curated bundles in the two priority regions, a straightforward booking and payment flow, and basic post-trip feedback capture. All other capabilities will be treated as post-MVP and tracked in A5.

Please make sure T4 and A1 are updated to reflect this so downstream teams have a clear scope boundary.

I will update the T4 notes to align with D2 and make sure the backlog entries that go into A5 are clearly tagged as MVP vs later.

I will also add a short comment on how we can phase in more advanced features after we see initial traction, so we do not lose sight of future opportunities while keeping the first release focused.

Once T1 and T4 are updated with D1 and D2, I will prepare a short internal summary for leadership and customer support so everyone understands who we are targeting and what will be in the first release.

I will also highlight that anything outside the confirmed MVP scope will be considered for later phases, to manage expectations.

Quick recap for this thread:
- D1: we confirmed two primary customer segments and two priority regions in existing markets.
- D2: we locked a lean MVP feature set focused on discovery, booking, payment, and basic feedback for curated bundles in those regions.

Next steps are to update T1, T3, T4, A1, and A4 accordingly and then feed this into the financial and go-to-market work.

Please post here once the docs are updated so we can reference them in the next planning sessions.

threads.thread_goal: Define and validate eco-tourism bundles, partner criteria, and service standards.

messages.text:
Starting a thread on curated bundles, partner criteria, and service standards.

I have a first draft for T2, T6, and T10. In short:
- For T2, I outlined 10 bundles across the two priority regions, each with clear inclusions, exclusions, and a sustainability angle.
- For T6, I drafted partner selection criteria based on environmental, safety, and community-benefit standards, aligned with A3.
- For T10, I started service standards for pre-trip, on-trip, and post-trip phases, which will later be formalised in A6.

I would like feedback from product and leadership before we lock which bundles go into the MVP catalog and finalise the criteria for pilot partners.

Thanks for sharing the draft. From a journey perspective (A4, T3), it would help if we can cluster the 10 bundles into a smaller number of themes for the MVP catalog.

For example, in each region we might have: 1) a soft-intro nature break for Segment 1, 2) a more immersive community-based stay for Segment 2, and 3) one family-friendly option.

Could you indicate which of the 10 bundles you see as the strongest fit for each segment and region so we can make a clear proposal for D3?

Looking at this from the MVP scope side (T4), we should be careful not to overload the first catalog.

If we can keep the MVP to maybe 3 to 4 bundles per region, that will simplify configuration and reduce the risk of fragmented experience, which was one of the risks in the project_pack_ref: Launch of Integrated Eco-Tourism Experience Platform.

I would also like to understand if any of the bundles require special booking flows or partner integrations that might stretch the MVP feature set we just agreed under D2.

From a commercial and pricing angle, some of the bundles in your draft will be easier to position than others.

I would prioritise bundles where inclusions and exclusions are very clear and where we can keep pricing competitive without undercutting community benefits. That will also make it easier to reflect them in A2 later.

Maybe we can score the 10 bundles quickly on clarity, sustainability strength, and margin potential, then pick the top ones for D3.

Good points. Based on the draft in T2, my suggestion for D3 is:

Coastal region:
- Bundle C1: 4-day marine conservation intro, guided snorkelling with local community guides, homestay, suitable for Segment 1.
- Bundle C2: 7-day marine and village immersion, including conservation workshops, for Segment 2.
- Bundle C3: 5-day family-friendly coastal nature break with lighter activities.

Forest or mountain region:
- Bundle F1: 4-day guided low-impact trekking with eco-lodges, for Segment 1.
- Bundle F2: 8-day community-based forest immersion with homestays, for Segment 2.
- Bundle F3: 5-day family-friendly forest discovery.

The remaining bundles in T2 can be kept as candidates for later phases.

This looks like a solid and focused set.

Before we confirm D3, I want to be sure that all six proposed MVP bundles can meet the partner criteria in T6 and the service standards in T10 without requiring exceptions.

Can you confirm that the operators behind C1 to C3 and F1 to F3 can comply with the environmental, safety, and community-benefit criteria you are drafting in A3 and that they can follow the service guidelines that will go into A6?

Yes, for the six proposed MVP bundles, we already work with partners who meet or are very close to the criteria in T6.

For A3, the checklist covers environmental practices, safety standards, and community involvement. These partners already have basic certifications and community agreements in place. We may need minor adjustments, but nothing that would block the MVP.

For T10 and A6, I will align the service standards with what these partners can realistically deliver in the first 90 days, while still raising the bar on pre-trip information, on-trip briefings, and post-trip feedback.

From the journey side, these six bundles give us a clear structure for A4.

We can design two main flows per region, with slight variations for family vs non-family travellers, without adding complexity to the platform.

I support using C1 to C3 and F1 to F3 as the MVP catalog for D3, as long as we clearly tag the others in T2 as post-MVP options.

From the MVP feature perspective, these six bundles are manageable.

We can configure them in the catalog with standard fields and avoid special flows. That keeps us aligned with D2 and the constraints in T4.

I would just ask that we avoid adding custom add-ons for the MVP, and instead keep any extras as simple notes or post-MVP backlog items in A5.

Given the alignment, I propose we confirm D3 as: the MVP catalog will include six curated bundles, C1 to C3 in the coastal region and F1 to F3 in the forest or mountain region, with all other drafted bundles in T2 reserved for later phases.

Please reflect this in T2 and in the partner and service documentation so there is no ambiguity for downstream teams.

Agreed on D3. I will update T2 to clearly mark C1 to C3 and F1 to F3 as MVP bundles and move the others into a separate section for future releases.

On D4, for partner selection and sustainability criteria, my proposal is that we adopt the full checklist in T6 and A3 for all pilot partners, without exceptions, and that we integrate a compliance review step into the product approval flow as described in T6.

From a commercial standpoint, applying the full criteria in T6 to all pilot partners is the right call, even if it limits the number of operators at first.

It will also make our positioning clearer in the go-to-market work and help justify pricing.

I support adopting the checklist in A3 as-is for D4, with the understanding that we may need to help some partners close small gaps before launch.

From the customer journey perspective, having a consistent partner standard via T6 and A6 is important to avoid fragmented experiences.

I support using the full checklist for D4, and I would like to ensure that the service standards in T10 and A6 explicitly cover pre-trip communication, on-site briefings, and post-trip feedback, since those are key touchpoints in A4.

Understood. I will make sure T10 and A6 emphasise those three phases clearly.

For D4, to summarise the proposal: all pilot partners for the six MVP bundles must meet the full environmental, safety, and community-benefit checklist in T6 and A3, and must commit to the service standards defined in T10 and A6. No bundle will go live without passing this review.

Let us confirm D4 as you summarised: all pilot partners for the MVP bundles must satisfy the full checklist in T6 and A3 and adhere to the service standards in T10 and A6, with a mandatory compliance review step before any product goes live.

This will be our baseline for partner selection and sustainability going forward.

Please ensure T6, T10, A3, and A6 are updated to reflect this and that the process is clear for operations and legal.

I will help by drafting a short internal note summarising D3 and D4 for leadership and for the partner management team.

I will pull from T2, T6, and T10 so that everyone understands which bundles are in the MVP and what criteria partners must meet.

Recap for this thread:
- D3: we selected six curated bundles, three per region, as the MVP catalog, with the remaining bundles in T2 reserved for later phases.
- D4: we approved partner selection and sustainability criteria based on the full checklist in T6 and A3, plus service standards in T10 and A6, with a mandatory compliance review before go-live.

Next, we will feed these decisions into pricing, financial modelling, and the go-to-market narrative.

threads.thread_goal: Lock pricing approach, financial assumptions, and budget envelope.

messages.text:
Starting the financials and pricing thread.

I have uploaded a preliminary version of the financial model for T5 and T9 into A2. It includes base, optimistic, and conservative scenarios for the first 12 months, using early assumptions on bundle pricing, occupancy, and marketing spend.

I need your feedback on: 1) the pricing strategy for the six MVP bundles, 2) key volume and margin assumptions, and 3) a realistic budget envelope for MVP build and launch marketing so we can confirm D5 and D6.

I have reviewed A2 briefly. The structure looks good, but I think we should revisit a few assumptions.

For D5, I would suggest a pricing strategy where we benchmark against comparable eco-tourism offers but maintain a small premium for the added sustainability and community impact, as long as we communicate that clearly in the go-to-market work.

On volume, the optimistic scenario in A2 might be a bit aggressive for the first 3 months, given we are launching a new platform and working with a limited set of bundles.

On pricing, I agree with a modest premium positioning, but we need to stay within the competitive range for each region.

For D5, I would propose we set target price bands per bundle type: intro, immersive, and family. Then we can adjust within those bands based on seasonality and partner costs.

I can work with 52126 to pull reference prices from existing eco-offers in those regions and feed that into A2.

I can provide reference pricing and partner cost ranges for C1 to C3 and F1 to F3.

We should also ensure that the pricing strategy does not undermine community benefits. Some of our partners rely on these trips as a key income source, so we need to balance competitiveness with fair compensation.

I will send you a short summary of current partner rates and typical margins so you can plug them into A2 and T5.

From a demand perspective, the base scenario in A2 seems reasonable if we assume a gradual ramp-up over the first 6 months.

However, I would recommend we keep the first quarter expectations conservative until we see actual conversion data from the journeys defined in A4.

For D5, I support a pricing strategy that sets clear price bands per bundle type, with a small premium for sustainability, and uses the conservative volume scenario as the main planning baseline.

Understood. I will adjust A2 so that the base scenario is closer to what we currently call conservative, and keep the optimistic case as a stretch view.

On pricing, let us align that we will use price bands per bundle type, with a modest premium for sustainability and community impact, as long as we can justify it in the narrative.

Once 263727 and 52126 provide the reference data, I will update T5 and share the revised model for a final check before we lock D5.

On the budget envelope for D6, we should also consider the constraints from the project_pack_ref: Launch of Integrated Eco-Tourism Experience Platform, especially the cap on initial marketing spend and the 90-day MVP build.

I suggest we separate the budget into two parts in T9: 1) MVP build and operations, and 2) launch marketing, with clear ceilings for each.

We can then check if the current assumptions in A2 fit within those ceilings or if we need to adjust scope or expectations.

I have pulled some reference prices and sent them your way.

For each bundle type, we now have a competitive range and a suggested target price that leaves room for partner margins and our own costs.

I recommend we set the MVP prices near the middle of the competitive range, then adjust after we see early demand and feedback.

The suggested target prices look acceptable from the partner side.

We should just make sure that any seasonal adjustments are communicated clearly to partners and customers, so there are no surprises.

I will confirm with the key operators that these price points work for them before we finalise D5.

With the updated data in A2 and the partner confirmation, I propose we lock D5 as follows:

Pricing strategy: price bands per bundle type (intro, immersive, family) set near the middle of the competitive eco-tourism range in each region, with a modest premium for sustainability and community impact. Volume assumptions: we use the current conservative scenario in A2 as our planning baseline, with base and optimistic scenarios kept for reference.

If there are no objections, I will mark D5 as confirmed and update T5 accordingly.

No objections from my side. Using the conservative scenario as the planning baseline is prudent, and the pricing bands align with the value we are designing into the journeys.

I will make sure the go-to-market messaging later reflects the sustainability and community aspects clearly so that the modest premium is understandable to customers.

Aligned on D5.

On D6, for the budget envelope, I suggest we set a firm cap for launch marketing that matches the pre-approved amount in the project constraints and a separate cap for MVP build that reflects what our delivery teams estimate for the scope in A5.

We should also include a small contingency line in T9 for unforeseen costs, but keep it modest to avoid scope creep.

I have updated T9 with two separate budget lines: one for MVP build and operations and one for launch marketing, both within the constraints we have.

For D6, I propose we confirm this as our budget envelope, with a small contingency of up to 10 percent on the build side only, subject to leadership review if we ever need to tap into it.

This should give us enough flexibility without encouraging uncontrolled scope changes.

I have checked the updated T9 summary. The split between build and marketing looks clear, and the contingency level seems reasonable.

I will prepare a short note for leadership summarising D5 and the proposed D6 envelope so they can formally endorse it as part of T12.

Let us confirm D6 as: the MVP build and operations budget and the launch marketing budget are set as per T9, within the pre-approved marketing cap and with up to 10 percent contingency on the build side, subject to leadership review before use.

I will update A2 and T9 to reflect this and bring it to the next leadership check-in for formal sign-off.

Recap for this thread:
- D5: we agreed on a pricing strategy using price bands per bundle type with a modest sustainability premium and set the conservative scenario in A2 as our planning baseline.
- D6: we confirmed a budget envelope for MVP build and launch marketing as defined in T9, with a limited contingency on the build side.

Next, we will align these with the backlog in A5 and the risk and governance work in T12.

threads.thread_goal: Prioritise backlog, define KPIs, and prepare handover to delivery teams.

messages.text:
Opening the backlog and KPI thread.

I have updated A5 with a first pass at MVP backlog priorities based on D1 to D3 and D5 to D6, and I drafted a KPI framework in A8 for T8. T11 is also started with a preliminary handover index.

We need to: 1) confirm the MVP backlog priorities for D7, 2) agree on the KPI set and dashboard requirements for D8, and 3) make sure T11 and T12 give delivery teams enough clarity on scope, risks, and governance.

Looking at A5, the structure is clear. For D7, I would suggest we keep the MVP backlog limited to what is strictly needed to support the journeys in A4 and the six MVP bundles.

We can tag anything related to advanced partner tools, loyalty, or complex analytics as post-MVP, even if they are already drafted as user stories.

On T11, we should also make sure each backlog item has a clear owner and that dependencies are visible for delivery teams.

From a commercial perspective, I would prioritise features that directly impact conversion and clarity of the offer.

In A5, that means catalog browsing, bundle detail pages with clear inclusions and exclusions, pricing display, and a smooth checkout.

I am comfortable pushing anything like promo codes or complex cross-sell to later phases, as long as we track them in the backlog.

On the tourism side, I would like to ensure that partner and service standards are represented in the backlog, but I agree they do not all need to be in the MVP.

For D7, I suggest we keep only the minimum partner-facing capabilities needed to configure the six MVP bundles and capture feedback, and leave more advanced partner dashboards for later.

We should also include at least one item to ensure that sustainability and community impact data can be captured and reported later, even if the reporting itself is basic at launch.

That aligns with how A5 is currently structured. For D7, my proposal is:

MVP backlog includes:
- Core customer flows: discovery, bundle selection, booking, payment, and basic feedback.
- Minimal partner configuration for the six MVP bundles.
- Basic data capture for key KPIs in A8 (conversion, satisfaction, impact proxies).

Everything else is tagged as post-MVP in A5 and T11.

On KPIs for D8, A8 currently lists acquisition, conversion, average order value, NPS or equivalent satisfaction metric, and a simple impact indicator per trip.

On D7, I support the approach of keeping the MVP backlog focused on the core flows and minimal partner configuration.

We should also ensure that any items required to meet regulatory or compliance needs are included in the MVP, even if they are not directly visible to customers.

On D8, I would like to see at least one KPI that tracks community benefit, even if it is a simple proxy at first, so we stay aligned with our mission.

For D8, we can add a basic community benefit indicator to A8, such as estimated local income generated per trip or number of community-led activities booked.

We will need to confirm with partners what data they can provide reliably at launch, but even a simple metric is better than none.

On T12, we should also define how often we review these KPIs post-launch and who owns each metric.

I can work with partners to identify which community-related data points they can share consistently.

For launch, we might start with a simple estimate of local income per trip and the number of community-led activities included in each booking.

I will feed this into A8 so that the impact KPIs are realistic and do not create extra burden for partners.

On the acquisition side, I would also like A8 to track at least basic channel-level performance, so we can see which acquisition channels are driving bookings.

Even if the dashboard is simple at launch, having source or campaign tags will help us optimise later.

This should not add much complexity to the MVP backlog if we keep the tracking lightweight.

Good point. I will update A8 to include basic channel attribution, and add a small backlog item in A5 to ensure we capture source or campaign tags in the booking flow.

With these adjustments, the KPI set for D8 would cover acquisition, conversion, average order value, satisfaction, and a simple community benefit indicator, plus basic channel performance.

Given the discussion, I propose we confirm D7 as: the MVP backlog in A5 is frozen to include only the core customer flows, minimal partner configuration for the six MVP bundles, basic data capture for the agreed KPIs, and any mandatory compliance items, with all other stories tagged as post-MVP in A5 and T11.

If there are no objections, we will treat this as the final scope for handover.

No objections from me. I will make sure A5 and T11 clearly mark which items are MVP and which are post-MVP, and that dependencies are visible for delivery teams.

This should help avoid scope creep during implementation.

Aligned on D7.

For D8, with the updates to A8, the KPI set now includes: acquisition by channel, conversion rate, average order value, satisfaction (NPS or similar), and a simple community benefit indicator. A8 also specifies data sources and owners for each KPI.

I propose we confirm this as the launch KPI and dashboard scope, with the understanding that we can iterate post-launch as we learn more.

I am comfortable confirming D8 with that KPI set and the dashboard requirements in A8.

This gives us a balanced view of growth, revenue, satisfaction, and community impact, without overcomplicating the initial analytics implementation.

Please ensure T8 and T12 reflect the ownership and review cadence for these KPIs.

I will help by documenting the KPI owners and the review cadence in T12, and by adding a short summary of D7 and D8 for leadership.

This will also be useful for the regular KPI and financial review ritual mentioned in our channel practices.

For T11, I will finalise the handover package index so that delivery teams have a single place to find A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, and A8, along with the decisions D1 to D8.

Once that is done, we should be ready for the handover walkthrough.

Recap for this thread:
- D7: we froze the MVP backlog in A5 to core customer flows, minimal partner configuration, basic KPI data capture, and mandatory compliance items, with all other stories tagged as post-MVP in A5 and T11.
- D8: we approved the KPI set and dashboard requirements in A8, covering acquisition by channel, conversion, average order value, satisfaction, and a simple community benefit indicator, with clear data owners and review cadence.

Next, we will complete T11 and T12 and schedule the handover session with delivery leads.

threads.thread_goal: Align on go-to-market narrative, channels, and launch milestones.

messages.text:
Starting the go-to-market and launch thread.

I have drafted A7 for T7, outlining the initial go-to-market narrative, proposed acquisition channels, and a high-level launch calendar. It is aligned with the strategy in A1 and the financial envelope in T9.

We need to: 1) agree on the primary acquisition channels for D10, 2) confirm a realistic launch date window and key external milestones for D9, and 3) ensure the plan fits within the budget and capacity constraints.

Looking at A7, I would prioritise three main acquisition channels for the MVP: 1) our own website and email base, 2) partnerships with selected eco-travel agencies, and 3) targeted digital campaigns in niche eco-travel communities.

Given the limited marketing budget in T9, we should avoid spreading ourselves too thin across too many channels.

For D10, I would propose we treat these three as primary and keep any broader brand campaigns for later phases.

From the tourism side, partnerships with eco-travel agencies and local operators are key.

We should also leverage existing relationships with community-based organisations to reach travellers who care about impact.

I support focusing on a small set of channels for D10, as long as we include at least one route that highlights the community and conservation stories behind the bundles.

From a financial and KPI perspective, concentrating on a few channels will also make it easier to track performance in A8.

We should ensure that the channels we pick for D10 can be instrumented for basic attribution, as we discussed in the KPI thread.

On timing for D9, we need to check that the proposed launch window in A7 leaves enough buffer after MVP build completion to test the flows and train partners.

In A7, I tentatively set the external launch window for about two weeks after the planned MVP build completion, to allow for internal testing and partner onboarding.

Key milestones include: 1) internal beta, 2) partner training sessions, 3) soft launch to a small segment of our existing base, and 4) public launch.

We should validate whether this timeline is realistic given the 90-day build constraint and the budget envelope in T9.

The structure of the milestones in A7 makes sense.

For D9, I want to be sure we have enough time for a proper go or no-go review before we commit to a public launch date. That means we should schedule a formal review after internal beta and partner training, with clear criteria.

If we can build that into the calendar and still stay within the 90-day window plus a short buffer, I am comfortable confirming the launch window.

I can help by drafting the criteria for the go or no-go review and making sure they align with the risks and governance cadence in T12.

We can include readiness checks on product, partners, support, and basic KPI tracking before we confirm the public launch date.

On D10, I still recommend we keep the primary channels to the three we discussed: own website and email, selected eco-travel agencies, and targeted digital campaigns in niche communities.

We can use the soft launch phase to test messaging and offers in these channels before scaling.

Any broader campaigns can be planned once we see early results and have more budget flexibility.

I agree with that channel focus for D10.

During partner training, we can also encourage partners to promote the platform through their own networks, but I would treat that as a secondary, organic channel rather than a primary one.

This keeps the core plan in A7 manageable while still leveraging local relationships.

I will adjust A7 to explicitly include a go or no-go review milestone between partner training and public launch, with criteria drawn from T12.

On timing, if we keep the MVP build within 90 days and allow two weeks for internal beta and partner training, the public launch window would fall roughly in weeks 14 to 15 from now.

This should give us enough time to test and adjust without slipping too far beyond the initial plan.

With that adjustment, I propose we confirm D9 as: the external launch window is set for approximately weeks 14 to 15 from now, following a 90-day MVP build, internal beta, partner training, and a formal go or no-go review as defined in T12.

We will treat the exact public launch date as conditional on passing the review, but this is the window we will communicate internally and tentatively to key partners.

Aligned on D9.

From a financial and KPI standpoint, this window also fits with the assumptions in A2 and the review cadence in A8 and T12.

We just need to make sure that any changes in scope or timing are reflected quickly in those artifacts.

On D10, to summarise the proposal: primary acquisition channels for the MVP launch will be 1) our own website and email base, 2) selected eco-travel agencies, and 3) targeted digital campaigns in niche eco-travel communities.

Secondary, organic promotion via partners and communities will be encouraged but not treated as a core channel in A7.

If everyone is aligned, we can confirm this and update A7 and T7 accordingly.

That summary matches what we discussed.
